title: One Year On, Operation Sindoor Reshapes How India Fights Terror
excerpt: The 88-hour precision campaign that destroyed Pakistani terror infrastructure now defines New Delhi's counter-terrorism playbook
body:
Exactly one year ago, India launched its most audacious military operation since the 1971 war. Operation Sindoor — an 88-hour precision campaign targeting terrorist infrastructure deep inside Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir — has fundamentally rewritten the rules of engagement on the subcontinent.

**The Trigger and the Response:**

The operation followed the devastating Pahalgam terror attack in May 2025, which killed dozens of civilians in the Kashmir tourist town. Rather than the measured diplomatic protests of years past, New Delhi chose overwhelming force. Coordinated strikes by the Indian Air Force, Army, and Navy hit 13 Pakistani air bases and 11 airfields, destroying aircraft on the ground and dismantling terror staging areas along the Line of Control. Over 100 terrorists linked to major attack networks were neutralised.

On May 7, the IAF released an 88-second video capturing the scale of the campaign — a deliberate echo of the operation's duration. Nearly 600 IAF and Army personnel ran an 88-hour commemorative relay through New Delhi's landmarks, concluding with a flag-in ceremony at Air Force Station New Delhi.

**A Doctrine, Not Just an Operation:**

What makes Sindoor significant beyond the body count is the doctrine it established. US military expert John Spencer noted that India achieved air superiority within 72 hours, a feat that demonstrated joint-force capabilities previously untested at this scale. Six pillars now define the Sindoor doctrine: precision execution, real-time intelligence integration, indigenous technology reliance, political resolve, diplomatic manoeuvring, and national unity.

The operation showcased India's growing self-reliance in defence. Indigenous missile systems, drones, and surveillance platforms formed the backbone of the campaign — a stark contrast to earlier decades of import dependency. Defence analysts are already speculating about what a potential "Sindoor 2" might look like, with advanced naval capabilities and next-generation missile systems likely playing larger roles.

**The Diaspora Dimension:**

For the 4.4 million Indian-Americans, many with family ties to Kashmir and border regions, the anniversary carries personal weight. Cross-border shelling during the operation damaged homes in Uri and Salamabad, displacing families that many NRIs still support financially. The operation also shifted how the diaspora engages with India's security narrative — from passive observers to active advocates in Washington policy circles, where India's right to self-defence became a bipartisan talking point.

**What to Watch:**

Prime Minister Modi and External Affairs Minister Jaishankar both updated their social media profiles to mark the anniversary, signalling that Sindoor remains central to India's strategic messaging. The next test will be whether this doctrine deters future attacks — or whether the escalation ladder has simply been raised.
